title: Pea Flower vs Lily Flower Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Dal, peas and groundnuts come from one plant family. Onions, aloe and tulips come from another. Diya asks what makes a pea plant and an onion so different, and the answer is in their flowers.

This topic is not in the current NCERT text but is in the ISC syllabus. You will see Fabaceae (old name Papilionoideae, part of Leguminosae): root nodules, pinnately compound leaves with a pulvinus and stipules, then a pea flower taken apart: the standard, two wings and keel (vexillary aestivation), nine plus one diadelphous stamens and one carpel that becomes a legume. Then a lily flower built ring by ring: six tepals, six epitepalous stamens and three fused carpels with axile placentation. A side by side comparison, a pause and think, six useful plants sorted into their families, the ten free stamens exam trap, an original floral formula question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions. This is Episode 48 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
